compiled_state.description:
## Context

The current tickets branch stores ticket event dirs flat at `tickets/<id>`, making the root tree about 270 KB and causing every single-ticket commit to re-emit that large root tree. W2 changes only the on-disk layout to reduce per-commit tree churn. S1 history reclaim, W1 batching, and any live shared-store cutover are out of scope.

## Scope

Implement a fan-out layout `tickets/<sha256-2>/<id>` for canonical ticket ids. New code must read legacy flat and sharded stores during the expand phase, preserve all ids/aliases/events, and provide an idempotent ensure-registry migration. Do not run this migration against the live shared `.tickets-tracker`; fixture/throwaway stores only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New ticket writes land at `tickets/<sha256-2>/<id>`; `tests/unit/test_store_sharded_layout.py` proves a fixture single-ticket mutation makes the top-level tree bytes at least 80% smaller than an equivalent flat layout.
- [ ] Alias, short-id, and full-id resolution are unchanged for flat, mixed, and migrated stores; `tests/unit/test_store_sharded_layout_heldout.py` plus existing resolver selectors prove this.
- [ ] Event replay/listing is unchanged for flat, mixed, and migrated stores; targeted reducer/list tests prove the same states are returned.
- [ ] The migration maps every flat ticket dir to its deterministic shard, leaves no flat ticket dirs behind, preserves identities/event bytes, and a second run makes no commit; `tests/unit/test_store_sharded_layout.py` proves this.
- [ ] An interrupted migration working tree with some already-sharded dirs resumes safely on rerun without identity loss or duplicate commits; `tests/unit/test_store_sharded_layout.py` proves this.
- [ ] Migration collisions are fatal and atomic: two source paths mapping to the same sharded target abort before any partial commit/move; `tests/unit/test_store_sharded_layout.py` proves this.
- [ ] Merge-as-union reconvergence still preserves both sides on a two-clone sharded fixture; `tests/unit/test_store_sharded_layout_heldout.py` proves both commits remain reachable.

## Implementation Plan

1. Add `rebar._store.ticket_layout` as the single layout owner: sha256 first-2-hex shard/relpath derivation, existing-dir resolution, ticket-path-to-tracker-root reverse derivation, deterministic ticket iteration, shard-container recognition, pinned-tree path parsing, shard-container mkdir, and `migrate_flat_ticket_dirs_unit`.
2. Writers create the shard container with `exist_ok=True` under the write lock before the atomic `os.rename(staging_dir, ticket_dir)`, preserving ticket+first-event atomic publication while an empty shard container remains benign; rollback/unpublish may leave an empty shard container, which fsck classifies as store data.
3. Keep resolver outputs separator-free. `_ids.py` returns ids/names only; exact lookup and prefix/alias scans build the same sorted id index from flat and sharded dirs through the layout helper.
4. Route all flat ticket path consumers through the helper. Required inventory: `_store/{staging,gitutil,store_usability,compat,ensures,env_identity,hlc}.py`; `reducer/{_api,_inbound}.py` (including `reduce_ticket` reverse derivation); `_ids.py`; `_engine_support/{field_reads,lookups,reads,validate,next_batch,commit_impact}.py`; graph `{_cache,_graph,_hierarchy,_links,_status,_unblock}.py`; _commands `{_seam,gates,doctor,composer,composer_edit,leaf,link_revert,unlink,claim,transition,transition_close,txn,delete,recent_creates,completion_candidate,compact,compact_plan,compact_rebuild,compact_recovery,compact_trigger,compact_txn,close_precheck,close_disposition,fsck_scan,fsck_repair,fsck_tracker_health,fsck_recover,fsck_authorship,fsck_restore,identity,session_log,tracker_maintenance,trusted_env_cmd,verify_authorship}.py`; sidecar/bot readers `{attest/authorship,attest/authorship_resolution,signing,metrics/{blame,event_metrics,sidecar_metrics,bug_trends},_snapshot/{ticket_view,ticket_objects},llm/{completion_sidecar,code_review/sidecar,overlap/queue,overlap/digest_sidecar,enrich_drain,plan_review/claimability,plan_review/relation_snapshot,plan_review/sidecar,epic_bug_screen,workflow/recorder},_io/{export_ndjson,import_ndjson},_engine/rebar_reconciler/{__main__,transition_replay,local_label_intent,impossible_links,inbound_translate,reconcile_check,apply_inbound_events,apply_inbound_records}}.py`.
5. Register ensure id `ticket-layout-shards` in `_store.ensures`. It runs under the write lock, precomputes all moves before mutation, refuses target collisions as fatal/permanent, treats already-sharded dirs as no-ops on rerun, stages old+new paths, and commits once only when drift exists. If killed after renames but before commit, no partial commit exists; rerun completes the mixed working tree or an operator can reset it; targeted tests cover this resume path.
6. Register required-capability token `sharded-ticket-layout` in `compat.KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` before any store stamps it. The migration appends that token so older v1.0+ binaries fail closed while current binaries read the store.
7. Make fsck/store-health depth-aware at shared `foreign_store_path_list` / `_holds_events`, so valid two-hex shard containers are store data even when empty and unrelated top-level dirs remain `FOREIGN_STORE_PATH`.
8. Update pinned snapshot readers to parse both `<id>/<event>` and `<shard>/<id>/<event>` through the layout helper.
9. Document the durable layout scheme, sha256 shard derivation, migration, and compat-token semantics in `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/migrations.md`.
10. Preserve expand-phase compatibility: before migration, readers handle both layouts and existing flat tickets may be updated in place; after migration, all tickets resolve to shards. Live cutover is deferred to the operator.
11. The migration holds the write lock for local filesystem renames and one local git commit only; no network push happens inside the lock. The live 6,008-ticket cutover is operator-scheduled for a maintenance window.
## Surface-Parity Census

- CLI: in scope via subprocess create/comment/show fixture tests.
- MCP/API: out of scope for live MCP because the server may run older code; accepted because tools delegate to the same library/core paths.
- Library: in scope via `import rebar` create/show/reduce tests.
- Automated callers: in scope through inventory updates and targeted unit selectors; no live Jira/LLM calls.
- Dual-direction: in scope for local read/write and import/export; outbound Jira field semantics unchanged.

## Testing / Verification

Run targeted RED/GREEN selectors: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_store_sharded_layout.py tests/unit/test_store_sharded_layout_heldout.py -q`, existing resolver/reducer selectors, and reconvergence/store path selectors. Final preflight: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test` with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on `PATH`.

## Deployment / Rollback

This change ships mechanism only. Applying it to the live shared store is an operator decision and is not performed here. After an operator migrates a store, rollback is a tickets-branch revert or approved tracker-maintenance action that restores flat paths, relocates any post-migration sharded ticket dirs back to flat paths, and removes the capability stamp together; tests assert that post-migration tickets remain resolvable after the compensating rollback. No agent force/bypass.

## Portability

In-process layout/migration only; no CI-provider dependency.
